use: With a negative it means 'not at all'; on its own it's an exasperated sigh.

example.ja: 彼の話、まったくわからなかった。
example.english: I didn't understand a word he said.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare no hanashi wa mattaku wakarimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の話はまったくわかりませんでした。
examplePolite.english: I didn't understand his talk at all.

notes: Mattaku mou! = honestly! (annoyed). Mattaku onaji = exactly the same.

use: Mostly sappari wakaranai (no idea at all); sappari shita describes light food or a fresh, clean feeling.

example.ja: この問題、さっぱりわからない。
example.english: I have no clue how to do this problem.

examplePolite.ja: この問題はさっぱりわかりません。
examplePolite.english: I don't understand this problem at all.

notes: Sappari shita aji = a light, refreshing taste.

use: A firm, total 'none': issai kankei nai (nothing whatsoever to do with it).

example.romaji: Sono ken ni wa issai kankei nai yo.
example.ja: その件には一切関係ないよ。
example.english: I have absolutely nothing to do with that.

examplePolite.romaji: Sono ken ni wa issai kankei arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: その件には一切関係ありません。
examplePolite.english: I have nothing whatsoever to do with that matter.

notes: Stiffer than zenzen; common in rules and notices.

use: A serious 'never' for promises and warnings.

example.romaji: Kono koto wa kesshite dare ni mo iwanai.
example.ja: このことは決して誰にも言わない。
example.english: I'll never tell anyone about this.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono koto wa kesshite dare ni mo iimasen.
examplePolite.ja: このことは決して誰にも言いません。
examplePolite.english: I will never tell anyone about this.

notes: Zettai ...nai is the everyday 'never'; kesshite sounds more solemn.

use: Usually about change or progress: daibu yoku natta, daibu nareta.

example.ja: 風邪、だいぶよくなったよ。
example.english: My cold's a lot better.

examplePolite.ja: 風邪はだいぶよくなりました。
examplePolite.english: My cold is much better.

notes: For a plain 'very' with an adjective, use totemo.

use: A state that has fully changed: sukkari wasureta, sukkari kawatta.

example.ja: ごめん、すっかり忘れてた。
example.english: Sorry, I totally forgot.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、すっかり忘れていました。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry, it completely slipped my mind.

notes: Don't mix with sukkiri (refreshed).

use: Stresses a high degree, often of something bad or impressive.

example.ja: 彼、相当怒ってたよ。
example.english: He was seriously mad.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa soutou okotte imashita yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は相当怒っていましたよ。
examplePolite.english: He was quite angry.

notes: After an amount it means 'worth': ichiman'en soutou (worth 10,000 yen).

use: Guesses at a high degree from what you see: yoppodo tsukareteru n da ne (you must be really tired).

example.romaji: Yoppodo onaka suiteta n da ne.
example.ja: よっぽどお腹すいてたんだね。
example.english: You must have been really hungry.

examplePolite.romaji: Yoppodo onaka ga suite ita n desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: よっぽどお腹がすいていたんですね。
examplePolite.english: You must have been very hungry.

notes: In comparisons, 'way more': kotchi no hou ga yoppodo ii (this one's way better). Casual form of yohodo.

use: The minimum you hope for or ask for.

example.romaji: Okureru nara, semete renraku shite yo.
example.ja: 遅れるなら、せめて連絡してよ。
example.english: If you're going to be late, at least let me know.

examplePolite.romaji: Okureru nara, semete renraku shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 遅れるなら、せめて連絡してください。
examplePolite.english: If you'll be late, please at least get in touch.

notes: Sukunakutomo is a factual 'at least'; semete is a wish or request.

use: A minimum estimate or fact.

example.ja: 少なくとも一時間はかかるよ。
example.english: It'll take at least an hour.

examplePolite.ja: 少なくとも一時間はかかります。
examplePolite.english: It will take at least an hour.

notes: Also 'at any rate': sukunakutomo watashi wa shiranakatta (I didn't know, anyway).

use: Usually with a negative to draw a line: kore ijou muri (I can't take any more).

example.ja: もうこれ以上食べられない。
example.english: I can't eat any more.

examplePolite.ja: もうこれ以上食べられません。
examplePolite.english: I couldn't eat another bite.

notes: After a number, ijou means 'or more': juunin ijou (ten or more people).

use: Picks out the most important point.

example.romaji: Nani yori, minna buji de yokatta.
example.ja: 何より、みんな無事でよかった。
example.english: Most of all, I'm glad everyone's safe.

examplePolite.romaji: Nani yori, minasan buji de yokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 何より、皆さん無事でよかったです。
examplePolite.english: Above all, I'm glad everyone is safe.

notes: Ogenki de nani yori desu = I'm so glad you're well (polite set phrase).

english: as hard as you can; your very best
use: Full effort within your limits; seiippai ganbaru.

example.ja: 精いっぱい頑張るよ。
example.english: I'll do my very best.

examplePolite.ja: 精いっぱい頑張ります。
examplePolite.english: I'll give it my all.

notes: Kore ga seiippai = this is all I can manage.

english: with all your might; to your heart's content
use: Holding nothing back: omoikkiri asobu, omoikkiri naku.

example.ja: 今日は思いっきり遊ぼう！
example.english: Let's have all the fun we can today!

examplePolite.ja: 今日は思いっきり遊びましょう！
examplePolite.english: Let's enjoy ourselves to the full today!

notes: Casual form of omoikiri.

use: Often otagai ni (to each other), or alone meaning 'we both'.

example.ja: お互い頑張ろうね。
example.english: Let's both hang in there.

examplePolite.ja: お互い頑張りましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's both do our best.

notes: Otagaisama desu = we're in the same boat (reply to thanks or an apology).

use: Managing despite difficulty: dou ni ka naru (it'll work out).

example.romaji: Dou ni ka ma ni atta.
example.ja: どうにか間に合った。
example.english: Somehow I made it in time.

examplePolite.romaji: Dou ni ka ma ni aimashita.
examplePolite.ja: どうにか間に合いました。
examplePolite.english: I managed to make it in time.

notes: Dou ni ka shite! = do something about it! Nantoka is a close, very common synonym.

english: exactly; a perfect fit; just right
use: A perfect match in size, timing or suitability: pittari no hito (the perfect person).

example.ja: この靴、サイズぴったり！
example.english: These shoes fit perfectly!

examplePolite.romaji: Kono kutsu wa saizu ga pittari desu.
examplePolite.ja: この靴はサイズがぴったりです。
examplePolite.english: These shoes are exactly my size.

notes: Also exact amounts or times: pittari sen'en (exactly 1,000 yen).

use: Casual 'perfectly done' or 'fully ready': junbi batchiri.

example.ja: 準備はバッチリだよ。
example.english: I'm all set.

examplePolite.ja: 準備はバッチリです。
examplePolite.english: Everything's ready.

notes: Pittari is about fit; batchiri is about things going or looking just right.

english: feel refreshed; feel better; look neat
use: Relief once something is off your chest or out of the way; also a tidy, uncluttered look.

example.ja: 全部話したらすっきりした。
example.english: I feel so much better after telling you everything.

examplePolite.ja: 全部話したらすっきりしました。
examplePolite.english: I feel much better now that I've said it all.

notes: Don't mix with sukkari (completely). Heya ga sukkiri shita = the room looks neat now.

use: A slip you didn't mean, often with -te shimau.

example.ja: うっかり乗り過ごしちゃった。
example.english: I accidentally missed my stop.

examplePolite.ja: うっかり乗り過ごしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I carelessly rode past my stop.

notes: Ukkari shiteta = I wasn't paying attention.
